subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Tooth Profile: The Involute Curve
description: A fast breakdown of Tooth Profile: The Involute Curve for builders.

hook.text: Gear teeth aren't shaped randomly. They follow a precise mathematical curve called an involute.

buildup.text: An involute is the path traced by unwinding a string from a circle. It creates a smooth rolling contact.

discovery.text: Involute teeth maintain a constant speed ratio even if the center distance isn't perfect. They're forgiving.

twist.text: Before involute gears, teeth were shaped by trial and error. Every gear pair had to be custom-matched.

climax.text: Today, any involute gear meshes with any other of the same pitch. Standardization made mass production possible.

punchline.text: One curve standardized all gears. Math beat guesswork.

quiz.question: Why is the involute tooth profile preferred for gears?
options: It eliminates all friction between meshing gear teeth
It maintains constant speed ratio even with slight center distance errors
It allows gears to operate without any lubrication
